div.head: Hu 6.1
div.ab: And gyf hine man teó, þæt he hine utsceóte, geladige hine swa hit on lande stande.
Et si compelletur (compellabitur), quod eum emiserit, allegiet se sicut uetus (in terra) lex est.
Qui si calumpnietur, quod eum effugere fecerit, purget se secundum legem patrie.
And gyf hine man teó, þæt he hine utsceóte, geladige hine swa hit on lande stande.
Und wenn dieser beschuldigt wird, dass er ihn fortgelassen habe, so reinige er sich, wie es im Land[recht] gilt.
And if this man is accused of having let him go, let him clear himself as is valid in the [law of the] land.
And if he is accused of abetting him in his escape, he shall clear himself according to the established custom of the district.
And if he is accused of abetting his escape, he is to clear himself according as it is established in the district.
div.note: B has an old point after ‘stande’; a hyphen (16th c.?) after it would join the start of 7 to this chapter.

note.seg: alter Punkt; Bindestrich [16. Jh.?] dahinter will den Anfang von Cap. 7 hierher beziehen; in Cap. 7 hat We grosse Initiale, die aber neu, auf Rasur
old point; a hyphen [16th cent.?] after it seeks to attach the beginning of cap. 7 to this; in cap. 7 We has a large initial, which is, however, later, on an erasure
before the bracket Lond; (bracketed) the others
‘wegführte’ Schmid zu stark. Vielmehr ‘bewusst entliess’ = tæce fram him II As 22, 2 = II Cn 28; vgl. Gl Begünstigung 15a
‘led away’ Schmid: too strong. Rather ‘knowingly let go’ = tæce fram him II As 22, 2 = II Cn 28; cf. Gl Begünstigung 15a
Ich berichtige meine durch Q beeinflusste Übs. ‘Landrecht’ in: ‘wie es dort zu Lande gilt’; vgl. Partikularrecht 7b. Da patria ‘Provinz’ heissen kann, meint Cons vielleicht das Richtige
I correct my translation ‘Landrecht’, influenced by Q, to ‘wie es dort zu Lande gilt’; cf. Partikularrecht 7b. Since patria can mean ‘province’, Cons perhaps has the right meaning
sicut in terra lex liest die Q-Hs. Rs wörtlich. Später scheint Q mit vetus richtig zu verstehen: ‘althergebrachten Brauch’, keinen Ggs. zu diesem neuen Statut
The Q MS Rs reads literally sicut in terra lex. Later Q seems to understand it rightly with vetus: ‘long-established custom’, not a contrast to this new statute
Cf. II Cn. 34 which points to the continuance till then of various types of procedure in different parts of the country.
